identity.name: Inkwell Jazz Festival
identity.one_line_description: Inkwell Jazz Festival is an annual outdoor celebration of jazz music told through a warm, illustrated world of hand-lettered stages, soulful lineups, and unforgettable summer nights.
identity.target_audience: Jazz lovers, live-music enthusiasts, and culture-seekers aged 25–55 who value authentic artistic experiences and seek a festival with soul, intimacy, and a distinct handmade character.

pages.title: Home
pages.goal: Welcome visitors with an unmistakable arrival moment that feels like opening a beautifully illustrated festival programme — establishing the Inkwell brand, the dates, and the emotional promise of the event, then guiding them toward the lineup and tickets.
pages.meta_description: Inkwell Jazz Festival — hand-drawn nights and live-played magic. Discover the lineup, explore the experience, and get your tickets for this summer's most soulful outdoor jazz celebration.

sections.intent: Anchor the visitor with an unmistakable arrival moment: a bold illustrated festival identity that feels like the ink is still wet on the poster, establishing the event name, dates, and the emotional promise of a singular jazz night under the open sky.
sections.headline: Where the music writes itself.
sections.subheadline: Three days. Forty artists. One hand-drawn world you'll never want to leave.

sections.intent: Draw the visitor into the soul of the festival with a lyrical editorial passage that explains what makes Inkwell different — its handmade spirit, its community roots, and the feeling of being inside a living illustration.
sections.headline: Born from a love letter to jazz.
sections.subheadline: Inkwell started as a sketch on a napkin. Eight years later, it's the most anticipated jazz weekend of the summer.
sections.body: We didn't set out to build a festival. We set out to build a feeling — the kind you get when a saxophonist closes their eyes and the whole crowd holds its breath. Every stage, every set, every hand-lettered sign at Inkwell is made with that feeling in mind. Come as a stranger. Leave humming something you've never heard before.

sections.intent: Close the home page with a confident final flourish — a warm, direct invitation to commit, reinforcing the scarcity of the moment and guiding the visitor to secure their place at the festival.
sections.headline: Don't let this summer pass in silence.
sections.subheadline: Early-bird passes are selling fast. Reserve your spot before the ink dries.

pages.title: Experience
pages.goal: Paint a rich, sensory picture of what it actually feels like to attend Inkwell Jazz Festival — the stages, the food, the workshops, and the atmosphere — so that first-time visitors feel they already belong there before they've bought a ticket.
pages.meta_description: Discover what awaits you at Inkwell Jazz Festival — three hand-crafted stages, artisan food villages, jazz workshops, and an atmosphere unlike any other outdoor music event.

sections.intent: Set the editorial tone for the Experience page with a warm, illustrative header that feels like the opening spread of a festival zine — slow and deliberate, inviting the visitor to settle in and read.
sections.headline: Three days drawn from the best of jazz culture.
sections.subheadline: From sunrise sessions to late-night jams, every moment at Inkwell is crafted by hand.

sections.intent: Reveal the festival's key experience pillars in a staggered scroll — each card arriving like a new page turning — so visitors build a complete picture of everything Inkwell offers beyond the music.
sections.headline: More than a concert. A whole world.

items.title: The Main Stage
items.description: Our flagship open-air stage hosts headline acts each evening as the sun sets over Riverside Meadows. Capacity for 8,000 — intimate enough to feel the music.

items.title: The Inkwell Tent
items.description: A candlelit marquee for late-night sets, experimental jazz, and surprise collaborations. Capacity is deliberately small. Arrive early.

items.title: The Sketch Stage
items.description: Our daytime acoustic stage celebrates emerging artists and local talent. Every set is free to attend with a festival wristband.

items.title: Jazz Workshops
items.description: Sit in on masterclasses led by performing artists. Improvisation, composition, and music history sessions run throughout the weekend.

items.title: The Food Village
items.description: Over 30 independent food vendors, craft breweries, and specialty coffee roasters — all curated to match the handmade spirit of the festival.

items.title: The Illustration Market
items.description: A dedicated marketplace of independent artists, printmakers, and record sellers. Take home something hand-drawn as a memory of the weekend.

asset_ideas.subject: A set of hand-drawn style icons representing: a stage/microphone, a tent, an acoustic guitar, a music note, a food bowl, and a paintbrush — each with a loose ink-line aesthetic
asset_ideas.purpose: Feature grid icons that visually reinforce the handmade aesthetic while identifying each experience pillar at a glance

sections.intent: Slow the scroll with a deliberate, ambient passage about the atmosphere and sensory texture of Inkwell — a moment of stillness that lets the visitor imagine themselves already there.
sections.headline: You'll smell the cedar smoke before you hear the first note.
sections.body: Inkwell is built for lingering. For the conversation that starts between sets. For the sketch you make on a paper cup. For the musician who plays an extra song because the crowd won't let them leave. We design every corner of the festival grounds the way a good album is sequenced — so that each moment leads naturally into the next, and the whole thing feels inevitable by the time it's over.

sections.intent: Convert the visitor who has now been fully seduced by the experience story — a single, warm, confident call to action that feels less like a sales push and more like a friend saying 'you really should come'.
sections.headline: Your weekend is waiting to be written.
sections.subheadline: Tickets are available in day passes and full weekend bundles.

pages.title: Lineup
pages.goal: Present the full artist roster in a way that feels like flipping through a beautifully hand-lettered festival programme — building excitement for every name on the bill and making it easy to discover new artists alongside the headliners.
pages.meta_description: Meet the artists of Inkwell Jazz Festival 2025 — headliners, emerging voices, and local legends performing across three stages over three unforgettable days.

sections.intent: Open the lineup page with the energy of a freshly posted festival bill — bold, celebratory, and hand-drawn in spirit — so that visitors feel the excitement of discovery from the very first scroll.
sections.headline: Forty artists. Three stages. Zero bad seats.
sections.subheadline: From jazz legends to the names you'll be telling your friends about next year.

sections.intent: Showcase the headline acts with the weight and presence they deserve — each name arriving with a staggered reveal that builds anticipation, like a poster being unveiled one artist at a time.
sections.headline: The names that draw the crowd.

items.title: Marlena Voss Quartet
items.description:
Friday Night · Main Stage · 9:00 PM
The voice that redefined contemporary jazz. Marlena's set promises material from her landmark album 'Indigo Hours' alongside new arrangements premiered exclusively at Inkwell.

items.title: The Coltrane Collective
items.description:
Saturday Night · Main Stage · 9:30 PM
A rotating ensemble of twelve musicians paying living tribute to the free jazz tradition. No two sets are the same. Expect the unexpected.

items.title: Esperanza Blue
items.description:
Sunday Night · Main Stage · 8:45 PM
Closing the festival with her signature blend of Afro-Cuban jazz and soul, Esperanza Blue brings the curtain down on Inkwell in the most joyful way imaginable.

sections.intent: Introduce the supporting acts and emerging artists with the same care and craft as the headliners — communicating that every slot at Inkwell is curated, not filled, and that discovery is part of the festival's promise.
sections.headline: The artists you'll discover this weekend.

items.title: Theo Adkins Trio
items.description: Friday · The Inkwell Tent · 7:00 PM — Modal jazz with a modern edge. Theo's piano work has been called 'the most interesting thing happening in jazz right now.'

items.title: Sable & the Horns
items.description: Saturday · Sketch Stage · 2:00 PM — A seven-piece brass ensemble rooted in New Orleans tradition. Daytime perfection.

items.title: Nora Kimani
items.description: Sunday · Inkwell Tent · 6:30 PM — Vocalist and composer whose debut EP sold out on vinyl in 48 hours. Her Inkwell set is her largest to date.

items.title: Riverside Collective
items.description: Saturday · Sketch Stage · 11:00 AM — Local heroes and Inkwell originals. The Collective has opened the festival every year since its founding.

sections.headline: Everything you need to know about where to go.

items.title: Main Entrance & Wristband Exchange
items.description: Located on Meadow Lane, Gate A. Open from 10:00 AM each day. Bring your ticket QR code or printed confirmation for wristband collection.

items.title: Main Stage
items.description: South-east corner of the meadow. Capacity 8,000. Gates open 90 minutes before each headline set. Accessible viewing platform available on the west side.

items.title: The Inkwell Tent
items.description: North of the Main Stage, 5-minute walk. Capacity 600. No reserved seating — arrive early for late-night sets.

items.title: Food Village & Bars
items.description: Central meadow, between the Sketch Stage and the Illustration Market. Open from 11:00 AM daily. Cashless payment only — top up your festival card at any info point.

items.title: Workshop & Talk Tents
items.description: North-west corner, adjacent to the Sketch Stage. Sessions run 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM each day. No booking required — just walk in.

items.title: Accessibility & First Aid
items.description: First Aid is located near Gate A and behind the Main Stage. Accessible entrances, viewing platforms, and quiet zones are marked in blue on the festival map.

sections.intent: Pre-empt the most common practical questions attendees have before arriving — reducing friction and building confidence so that visitors feel fully prepared and excited rather than anxious.
sections.headline: Questions we've already answered for you.

items.title: Can I bring my own food and drink?
items.description: Sealed water bottles and small snacks are welcome. Glass containers, alcohol, and large cool boxes are not permitted on the festival grounds.

items.title: Is there parking on site?
items.description: Yes — Meadow Car Park is a 10-minute walk from Gate A. We strongly encourage the use of our shuttle bus service from Riverside Station, which runs every 20 minutes from 9:00 AM.

items.title: Is the festival accessible for wheelchair users?
items.description: Inkwell is fully accessible. Accessible viewing platforms are available at all three stages, and accessible toilets are located throughout the site. Contact us in advance to arrange any additional support.

items.title: What happens if it rains?
items.description: Inkwell is an all-weather festival. The Inkwell Tent and Workshop Tents provide covered areas. We recommend layers and waterproofs — the music plays regardless.

items.title: Day Pass
items.description:
Single-day access to all stages and the festival grounds. Choose Friday, Saturday, or Sunday at checkout.

• Access to all three stages
• Illustration Market entry
• Festival programme included

items.title: Weekend Bundle
items.description:
Full three-day access — the best way to experience everything Inkwell has to offer without missing a note.

• All Day Pass inclusions × 3 days
• Priority entry each morning
• Exclusive weekend wristband

items.title: VIP Weekend
items.description:
The complete Inkwell experience, elevated. Includes everything in the Weekend Bundle plus access to the VIP Lounge, artist meet-and-greet sessions, and a signed festival print.

• All Weekend Bundle inclusions
• VIP Lounge access
• Artist meet & greet (two sessions)
• Signed limited-edition festival print

items.title: Under-16 Day Pass
items.description:
Children aged 8–15 accompanied by a ticketed adult. Under-8s enter free.

• Single-day access
• Must be accompanied by a full-price ticket holder
